payload.name: Preserve distinct stated impacts during memory extraction
payload.description: When extracting or updating a memory from a message where the speaker states multiple distinct impacts, reactions, or takeaways, apply this Skill to keep each explicit concept instead of merging them into one paraphrase.
content: During candidate extraction and when updating an existing memory, compare the candidate against the source message for explicitly stated distinct impacts, effects, or takeaways.
If the speaker names more than one distinct concept, preserve each one as its own clause or as a separate candidate; do not let one paraphrase subsume another.
Use the speaker's own named terms where possible, and stop once every explicitly stated distinct concept is represented; do not add inferred or exhaustive extra detail.

solves: The general failure is extraction paraphrase loss: when a user's message names several distinct impacts, effects, or takeaways, the candidate memory merges them and drops one, so later questions about the omitted concept cannot be answered. This Skill applies when constructing or updating memories from any statement listing more than one explicit reaction, impact, or thematic takeaway, and instructs preserving each stated concept. It does not apply to single-concept statements or to adding inferred detail not explicitly named.
